page: Amazon Web Services m5zn.12xlarge is a general-purpose, network-optimized compute instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The server is powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8252C x86_64 processor delivering 24 physical cores and 48 vCPUs with a sustained clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The CPU cache architecture includes 32 KB L1 data cache per core, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and a shared 24 MB L3 cache. It supports extended instruction sets including AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, AES, and FMA. Memory capacity totals 192 GB of DDR4 RAM operating at 3 GHz, preserving a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio.

The instance includes no bundled local storage, relying entirely on network-attached storage architectures, but provides a 100 Gbps baseline network throughput. Performance testing indicates strong results in uncached large-block memory throughput, recording 232.82 GB/sec read and 97.66 GB/sec write bandwidth. Compute testing reflects high single-thread compression efficiency at 31.93 GB/sec in gzip, strong Clang software compilation scores, and an overall PassMark CPU score of 48931.14. CPU-bound LLM text generation benchmarks exhibit lower throughput, reflecting typical limitations of running generative inference workloads on CPU architectures lacking hardware accelerators.

The hardware balance makes the m5zn.12xlarge cost-efficient for workloads that demand both high per-core processor clock frequencies and broad networking bandwidth without paying for unneeded GPU silicon. The absence of integrated NVMe disks necessitates reliance on external volumes for stateful services. This profile is best aligned with continuous integration pipelines, software compilation servers, network-bound web serving fleets, gaming servers, and general-purpose enterprise application backends requiring stable high-frequency execution.
description: Amazon Web Services m5zn.12xlarge is a high-frequency general-purpose instance driven by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. Equipped with a 48-vCPU Intel Xeon 8252C processor operating at 4.5 GHz and 192 GB of DDR4 memory, it delivers a balanced 1:4 compute-to-memory configuration alongside 100 Gbps baseline network connectivity. The system contains no bundled local storage, requiring external block storage. Benchmark assessments show strong memory bandwidth, with large-block uncached reads reaching 232.82 GB/sec, alongside top-tier Clang compilation performance and strong PassMark CPU evaluation results. While CPU-based generative LLM text generation is inherently limited due to the absence of dedicated accelerators, the instance provides high efficiency for high-clock-rate parallel tasks. The server is well suited for code compilation, continuous integration and build pipelines, gaming backends, high-throughput network applications, and general-purpose enterprise workloads.
